newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GOLF-LANGER GRABS SHARE OF LEAD IN DUNHILL MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER GRABS SHARE OF LEAD IN DUNHILL MASTERS.

text.p: Germany's Bernhard Langer, anxious to end a 13-month spell without a win, shot a four-under-par 71 on Friday for a share of the lead at the halfway stage of the Alfred Dunhill Masters.
His co-leaders were Paul Devenport of New Zealand, round in 70, Taiwan's Hsieh Yu-shu (66) and Park No-seok of South Korea (67).
"My putting was not as good as yesterday but I chipped well," said Langer, twice winner of the U.S. Masters.
"Every win is nice but victory here will not make up for missing out in Europe this year. It would certainly be good to win to end the season on a positive note and get my confidence back."
Langer failed to win a European Tour event this season for the first time in 17 years.

European number one Colin Montgomerie, still suffering the effects of jet-lag, carded his second successive 69 to lie five behind the leaders while South Africa's Ernie Els, three times World Matchplay champion, added a 69 to his first-round 71.
Troubled Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros of Spain bettered his opening 71 by one stroke but said he was still not striking the ball with confidence.
